text:
Winnipeg arrives with the better underlying numbers. The Jets generate 2.9 expected goals per 60 and allow 3.3, while Chicago sits at 2.6 for and 3.61 against, and the Blackhawks have been outchanced in their recent games, with just 38 percent of the five-game expected goals share. The model projects 3.04 goals for WPG and 2.82 for CHI. On special teams, the Jets' power play (0.66 expected goals per game) is twice as dangerous as Chicago's (0.32), and Chicago takes 3.43 penalties a game, which gives that edge room to matter.

The projected goalie matchup leans Winnipeg too. Stuart Skinner has a .920 save percentage and 3.44 goals saved above expected through four games, after 5.96 over 50 games last season. Spencer Knight, projected for Chicago, is at .890 and minus 0.34 this year, though he was well above average last season at plus 11.11 over 55 games, so a rebound is plausible.

Both teams played Tuesday. Winnipeg beat Minnesota 5-2 after a 5-1 loss to Anaheim, and Chicago beat Pittsburgh 5-3 but has allowed four or more goals in three of its last five. Among the players the model likes, Kyle Connor leads the board at 43 percent to score, with Mark Scheifele at 33 percent. For Chicago, Connor Bedard is the best bet at 33 percent to score and 28 percent for two or more points.
